judgements.lens:
Priorities 1 (correctness of outcome) and 2 (quality/simplicity of code). I scored each candidate on: does the pain it names survive a read of the evidence; does the mechanism actually bite that pain; and does it make wrong outcomes rarer rather than cheaper. Verification I ran: re-derived PP5 with one meter walk (`--by agent,model`: main Opus 28,273,671 out / 30,147 req; workflow-subagent Opus 12,835,327; general-purpose Sonnet 4,002,346 out / 4,346 req vs Opus 3,334,562 / 5,265 — draft's figures re-derive, corpus has since grown); read `_data/tokens-by-effort.json` (73,945 of 76,259 req at xhigh = 97%), `tokens-by-lane.json` (main cacheRead 10.34B/13.92B = 74%, 282,213 per request), `tokens-compactions.json` via 10-token-meter.md (107 distinct, all manual, min 462,618), `tokens-blocks.json`; read all 31 refuter verdicts and the completeness critique; and checked the live config myself — `bun not found`, `claude-mem@thedotmack` enabled and a Bun project (`bunfig.toml`), 1,020 `permissions.allow` entries, 43 `additionalDirectories`, `Bash(git reset:*)` and `Bash(for f:*)` present.

Four structural notes the draft does not carry. (1) The census's decisive finding for ranking is that only FOUR of 31 nominations survived refutation, and two of those four were confirmed under a different kind than nominated — so the dominant measured failure in this operation is claims that do not survive a read, not tokens. That puts C5, C4 and C11 above everything token-shaped. (2) `permissions.deny` is EMPTY (0 entries). C13 aims at the allow list; the correctness half — deny rules for the three incident-grade must-nots that 13-research §Rejected says are in the wrong layer (never commit from the main checkout, never bare `git stash`, never `git merge starter/main`) — is unwritten and unmentioned. (3) C1 and C9 are the same change (disable a plugin whose hooks fire on every event and do nothing) and should ship as one diff, with C9's token claim held back until its own A/B runs — 12-startup-cost.md states in bold that the ~53k opening cannot be attributed from transcripts. (4) C5's "the script exists" is true only of `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../census-refute.workflow.js`; `.claude/workflows/` does not exist in this worktree, so the two hours is real work gated on operator decision #7.

Where the blocks data cuts against the draft: 10-token-meter.md shows the three "high block" days are ONE stop each fanned across parallel subagents (64 blocks = 4 distinct minutes, 1 message text), and in local time the operator was stopped on five days, not eleven. PP3 is therefore smaller than its 243 headline suggests, which lowers C3's resumable-harness half and C6.

scores.reason: PP6/PP7. Verified independently, not just cited: `bun not found` on PATH, `claude-mem@thedotmack` enabled in `~/.claude/settings.json`, and the plugin ships `bunfig.toml` — a Bun-based hook layer on a machine with no Bun. Six hook events fire per session plus PostToolUse on every call, each first spawning `$SHELL -lc`; 216 hook errors in this session's transcript, 88 transcript files carrying the string, against 3 MCP tool calls in 30 days. This is an instrument that has only ever failed, running on every tool call — the exact class the repo's own rule is written about, and its steady non-blocking errors train a session to ignore hook output. 5 minutes, reversible, strictly simplifying. Not 5 because the context cost of the 216 error attachments is counted but never sized, so the token benefit is asserted, not measured.

PP2. Rests on one confirmed episode (verdict 25, 2026-08-24, wasteShare 0.6, 759,123 cacheRead in the tail window) plus the r=0.56 between limit blocks and concurrent breadth. The mechanism fit is honest in a way the draft undersells: the overload was SIX parallel agents, under the binding default of 10 (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY`, DOC-CONFIRMED), so only a lower cap would have bound — which is why step one is the experiment to find which cap binds. A deterministic env cap beats a remembered runbook under priority 1, and the cost is measured: 31 candidates at CHUNK=4 ran in 7m54s. Deductions: n=1 confirmed harm, the value 4 is a guess until the experiment runs, and the same cap slows the refuter rounds that produce correctness.

PP2/PP3. The stop-runbook half is the strong half and is pure priority 1: the docs say `Ctrl+X Ctrl+K` twice within 3s (DOC-CONFIRMED, interactive-mode.md:22) while the community source says `Ctrl+F` (PRACTICE-none), and verdict 25 shows the session spent 4 of its 6 TaskStop calls on a ToolSearch to load the TaskStop schema at the moment of the emergency — the mechanism was unread when it was needed. 30 minutes retires a contradiction rather than writing a runbook line on top of it. The resumable-harness half is thinner than drafted: exactly one confirmed archaeology episode (verdict 21, wasteShare 0.2 of a 25,457-out window) and one confirmed episode whose measured cost is literally 0 (verdict 29). Scored on the strong half.

PP4, the best-measured failure mode in the whole package: 16 of 40 lever claims refuted on the docs, 27 of 31 census nominations refuted on read, 3 of 3 S1 brief claims wrong on contact with 2 already sitting in fleet memory, and the sharp worker that re-derived a known fact for 169k tokens. Both controls were already observed today (S3's worker cited the memory file after the step was added; S1's did not without it), so the instrument has passed on a known-good input before any failure of it is reported. One hour to write, zero to run, ≤20 lines, and it serves 1, 2, 3 and 5 at once by killing the pasted-result path into the main lane. Stronger than a CLAUDE.md rule because it lives in the dispatch prompt rather than ambient context, which is exactly the placement 13-research §Rejected argues for.

PP4/PP7. The highest-yield instrument this week produced, and it has already passed and failed on real inputs: 27 of 31 nominations refuted, and it did not merely reject — it corrected the census's own labels on two of the four survivors (verdicts 21 and 29 both came back with `betterKind: continue-after-block`), and its completeness critic produced the ten blind spots including the instrument-blind class the census cannot see. Measured cost of a full round: 32 agents, 1,981,897 subagent tokens, 474s wall. Every evidence package so far has failed first refutation, which makes a standing round the cheapest defence against shipping a wrong claim to the operator. The script is 94 lines, single-purpose and readable (priority 2). Deduction acknowledged and correctly stated by the draft: run it only where the evidence is on disk, or the skeptics refute from priors.

PP1/PP3. Premises are measured — 282,213 cacheRead per main-lane request, Fable's own meta-week session at 374k, the 5h window proven end-to-end from two consecutive block messages (19:50→00:50) — but the mechanism serves 3, 4 and 5, not 1 or 2, and the draft says so. Its correctness contribution is indirect (see the window before launching a fan-out), and the blocks data shrinks the pain it points at: in local time the operator was stopped on five days in thirty, and the three high-block days are one stop each fanned across subagents. What keeps it at 3 rather than 2 is the proof step — dump the raw statusline JSON and read it before writing a single conditional against `context_window.used_percentage` — which is the house rule applied correctly to an unverified payload.

PP5. The premise re-derives from my own meter walk: 97% of 76,259 requests at xhigh, workflow-subagent 28.4% of all output on Opus (12,835,327), general-purpose Sonnet 4,002,346 out over 4,346 requests against Opus 3,334,562 over 5,265. But every one of those is a SIZE fact; nothing in the corpus measures whether Sonnet/medium reaches the same verdict, so the lever is a priority-5 saving aimed straight at the priority-1 surface. It stays at 3 because the guards are real and specific: judges stay on Opus, mechanical stages only, the A/B carries a deliberately hard FAIL control (the vida episode where the anchor was wrong), and it correctly refuses `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` globally on the documented pre-2.1.251 resolution order. Ship the A/B, not the change.

PP1. The premise is measured — 282k per request, 107 distinct compactions all `manual`, none below 462,618, p50 491,829 — but the payoff is explicitly NOT FOUND: 13-research §Not found states that how cache-read is weighted against the subscription limit is undocumented anywhere, so 'cache-read is where the tokens go' and 'cache-read is where the limit goes' are different claims and only the first is established. Worse for this lens, the census found zero confirmed redo after compaction (0 of 19 nominations survived), so the current compact-by-default habit has no measured correctness cost to repair, while `/clear` at a seam has a real state-loss failure mode. A priority-5 change with an unmeasured payoff and a priority-1 downside. Held at 2 rather than 1 only because it is framed as an A/B with a noise baseline (Aug 24–28 vs Sep 7–11) rather than as a rule.

PP6. Two halves with very different evidence. Disabling `claude-session-driver` — hooks on PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionStart/SessionEnd emitting events for a `csd` tmux worker with no recorded use — is the same sound move as C1 and should ship in the same diff. The token half is not established: 12-startup-cost.md states in bold that which of the system prompt, the 121-skill listing, three MCP servers' tool definitions, CLAUDE.md or the memory index accounts for the ~53k frontier opening 'is not answered here and cannot be answered from transcripts alone.' So the 84.4M-across-2,682-spawns headline does not attach to this mechanism until the scratch-session A/B runs. Correctly designed (numbers from the transcript, not `/context`; re-enable as the FAIL control), but do not present the saving before the A/B.

PP7 is real and well-evidenced (#782's `Analytics soft-fail at` field absent so the digest signal can never fire; #780's unset-output guard; the 08-12 trio). The mechanism is not. A CI check that fails a PR body lacking the strings 'PASS' and 'FAIL' cannot read evidence, so its green is satisfiable by typing two words — an instrument whose verdict carries no information, which is precisely the class it is meant to police. The draft concedes this ('it enforces the habit, not the truth') and still credits it with priority 1. Under priority 2 it adds a fourteenth workflow and a path-scoping surface to maintain for a condition no author can fail on purpose. C11 does the same job where it can actually be proven.

The only candidate aimed squarely at PP7, the class the census explicitly cannot see and the class behind every mistake CLAUDE.md records: a gate built on `report --preview` that did no IO and so could never pass, a VERDICT line grepping the wrong command, 18 PRs called 'stuck' under a rule working as designed. Its controls discriminate in both directions — PASS lists the never-fired `Analytics soft-fail at` signal, FAIL does not list `FLEET_FORM_E2E skipped=N`, which varies since #779 — so the instrument is proven on a known-good input before any verdict of it is trusted. The substrate exists: machine lines emitted from six files (`src/audits/smoke.ts`, `src/cli/commands/protection-audit.ts`, and four more) across 13 workflows, and the ack-with-expiry answer to a legitimately-invariant gate already ships as the Prismic drift ack. A day is the largest effort in the set and it is the right day. One gap to close before it fires: a minimum-run threshold, or every young check chips as 'unproven' purely on run count, and Actions log retention bounds N.

The measurement already refutes the mechanism, and the draft files that as a 'Mistake if' rather than as a disqualifier. Verdict 29 confirms the repeated `/model opus[1m]` turn was typed into three UNRELATED repos inside two minutes — Broken, beachfront-dentistry and reddoor-maintenance — which is a per-week reset behaviour, not a per-repo preference; and of the 81 switches, 26 went to `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` after 'we just got a reset'. A per-repo default key cannot fix a per-week trigger; it would fire on the wrong axis and add a settings file per repo to keep in sync. It also depends on operator decision #7 (`.claude/` tracking) being made first. Serves 3 at best, and only if the premise were true.

The pain is real and I verified it directly: 1,020 `permissions.allow` entries, 43 `additionalDirectories`, `Bash(git reset:*)` and `Bash(for f:*)` both present. But the draft aims at the wrong half. `permissions.deny` is currently EMPTY, and 13-research §Rejected already concluded the incident-grade rules are in the wrong layer — never commit from the main checkout, never bare `git stash`, never `git merge starter/main` — quoting 'CLAUDE.md is guidance... Never rely on it for anything that must not happen.' Adding those three deny rules is the priority-1 move and is not in the candidate. Meanwhile 'prune to patterns' walks into two documented silent failures: an unanchored allow glob is skipped with a warning, and a settings-file `mcp__` rule containing parentheses is skipped silently — so a prune can quietly remove protection or quietly remove permission. The drafted proof (a `git reset --hard` now asks) tests only the removal, never that the surviving patterns still allow what they should. 3 as written; a 4–5 rewritten as 'add the three deny rules first, then prune, with both directions proven.'

PP9. Part (a) is one CLAUDE.md line and nearly free, but its tie to the evidence is inferred rather than measured: the one confirmed overload (verdict 25) is six parallel agents, and the 'computer crashed because I also opened steam' turn sits among the 27 REFUTED nominations — so the browser-contention story has no confirmed episode behind it and the confirmed one is C2's territory. Part (c) is argued against by the package's own research: Option B 'cannot reach any relief from the binding constraint, because the ceiling here is the plan's usage limit rather than RAM,' and it forces copying credentials the sandbox already fences off (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/reddoor-maint`) onto an always-on box. Half a day of spike for a conclusion 13-research has already reasoned to. (b) Remote Control is minutes and harmless. Serves 3 and 4; nothing here moves 1 or 2.

demote: C12 — the draft lists it as serving priority 3 and files its killer as a 'Mistake if'. The evidence already refutes it: verdict 29 confirms the repeated `/model opus[1m]` was typed into three unrelated repos (Broken, beachfront-dentistry, reddoor-maintenance) inside two minutes, and 26 of the 81 switches went to Fable after 'we just got a reset' — a per-week trigger a per-repo default cannot address. It also waits on operator decision #7. Should be last, or moved to §3 'Not recommended'.

C10 — credited with priority 1, but the mechanism greps a PR body for the strings 'PASS' and 'FAIL'. It cannot read evidence, so its green is satisfiable by typing two words; that is a check whose verdict carries no information, the same class as #782's never-firing analytics signal and the 08-12 preview gate. The draft concedes it 'enforces the habit, not the truth' and scores it anyway. C11 does the same job at a layer where it can actually be proven, so C10 should rank below C11 and below C13, not adjacent to them.

C14(c) — the Linux-box spike. The draft scores C14 on priorities 3 and 4, but the package's own research already answers it: 'the ceiling here is the plan's usage limit rather than RAM,' so a second machine relieves nothing that is binding, and it forces the credential story the sandbox deliberately fences (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/reddoor-maint`). Keep (a) and (b) at near-zero cost; drop (c) below everything in §2 until a measurement says RAM or uptime is the constraint. Also note (a)'s stated pain has no confirmed episode — the steam crash is among the 27 refuted, and the one real overload (verdict 25) was six parallel agents, i.e. C2.

C8 — listed as 'Serves: 5, possibly 1'. The 'possibly 1' should come off. The census produced zero confirmed redo-after-compaction from 19 nominations, so the current manual-compact habit has no measured correctness cost, while `/clear` at a seam has a real state-loss mode. And its priority-5 payoff is explicitly NOT FOUND — 13-research states no source gives cache-read's weight against a Max-plan limit — so the lever's benefit is unmeasured in the one dimension it claims. Rank it below C7 among the token levers, and run it only as the A/B it is drafted as.

C9 — the headline number should not travel with the recommendation. 12-startup-cost.md states in bold that the ~53k frontier opening cannot be attributed from transcripts, so '84.4M across 2,682 spawns' does not attach to disabling plugins until the scratch-session A/B runs. Demote the token claim to a hypothesis; promote and merge its `claude-session-driver` half into C1, since both are 'remove a hook layer that fires on every event and does nothing' and should be one reversible diff the operator applies once.

judgements.lens: Priorities 3 and 4: ergonomics for future humans and agents, and work done between operator prompts. I scored each candidate on how much it lowers the operator's attention cost per unit of work, and how far a session can run unattended without losing state — judged against the full priority order, so a candidate that buys tokens (5) or minutes (6) at the cost of correctness (1) or of a stop-per-hour (4) scores below a free habit change that serves 1 and 3 together. Two things moved scores hard in both directions. First, the package's own instrument rule: a lever whose mechanism is asserted rather than read scores low however good its pain point is (C3, C10). Second, the meter's own warning that limit-block COUNTS are fan-out counts — 64 blocks on 2026-09-02 are one wall hit by 58 subagents in five minutes, and in local days the operator was stopped on five days, not eleven, and once on 09-06 rather than 53 times — which makes the r=0.56 correlation behind the fan-out case substantially mechanical and takes the air out of C2. The number I weighted most heavily for priority 4 is one the draft never quotes: the three exact session windows show the wall arriving 1h20m, 1h37m and 2h28m into a five-hour window (512,180 out in 80 minutes on 09-06), so elapsed time is not a usable heuristic for when a fan-out will survive, and only a live gauge or a slower burn is.

scores.reason: PP6/PP7. Measured: 216 hook errors in this session's transcript, 88 transcript files carry the 'Bun not found' string, each claude-mem hook first runs $SHELL -lc (a login shell) per tool call against a corpus of 93,080 tool calls, and its MCP tools were called 3 times in 30 days. Five minutes, reversible, and it is the repo's own rule applied to itself: an instrument that has only ever failed, firing on every call. Ergonomics gain is per-session and permanent — the error attachments stop entering context and the per-call shell spawn stops. Held at 4 not 5 because only 88 of ~3,300 transcript files carry the string, so the breakage may be recent and the month-long per-call tax is an upper bound, and because the sandbox denies writes to ~/.claude/settings.json so it costs one operator action.

PP2, and the evidence is thinner than the draft implies. One confirmed episode (2026-08-24, wasteShare 0.6) whose refuter explicitly places the avoidable decision — dispatching six agents — OUTSIDE the costed window ('the window captures the tail of the waste, not its cause'), and the r=0.56 correlation, which 10-token-meter.md undercuts: blocks are fan-out counts, not events. Worse for my lens, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY caps read-only tools as well as subagents (env-vars.md:303), so a global '4' throttles parallel Read/Grep in every session on the machine — an ergonomics regression paid in every session forever, bought with one episode. The per-dispatch half is free and proven (31 candidates, 4 at a time, 7m54s wall): keep CHUNK=4 in Workflow scripts, and hold the global env var until the binding-cap experiment actually runs.

The pain is well measured — 11 resumes from 243 block records, lags 57 to 211 minutes, two confirmed re-orientation episodes (i=21 JSONL archaeology, i=29 five Godot scripts re-read) — but the MECHANISM rests on no measurement and no doc citation anywhere in the package: 'journal.jsonl' and 'resumeFromRunId' appear nowhere in 13-research.md, and neither is on the verify list. Its own cited episode contradicts it: i=21's quote is 'The workflow finished but the session limit killed most of the verify lanes' — a Workflow that lost its lanes anyway — while the draft describes that episode as bare Agent fan-out 'with no journal'. The proof plan verifies the stop chord and TaskStop, which the census prices at almost nothing (spend-after-stop: 4 candidates, out 8,667 total, only 3 genuine, and the confirmed one's post-stop spend was in-flight and unrecallable), and never verifies the load-bearing claim. Routing also touches less than the draft suggests: 1,793 of 2,682 spawns already run as workflow-subagent. Add the missing control — kill a run mid-flight with lanes outstanding, resume by run id, show the finished lanes are not re-run — and this becomes a 5.

PP4 and PP1, and the only candidate that is free to run and already carries both controls observed in the same session: S3's worker cited the memory file after the step was added; S1's worker re-derived at 169k tokens without it; 2 of 8 workers today rediscovered facts already in fleet memory, and 3 of S1's brief claims were wrong on contact with 2 of them already in memory. 'Return a path plus a <=15-line summary' is the direct counter to main-lane 282k cached tokens re-read per request (74% of all cache reads), and it is also what makes a fan-out's results survive a limit block at all, since the artifact is on disk rather than in a context the wall destroys. Ergonomics is the whole point: one tracked template under 20 lines that shapes every future dispatch by human or agent, not one session's behaviour.

PP4/PP7, with the highest measured yield in the package: 27 of 31 census nominations refuted, 16 of 40 lever claims refuted on the docs, 3 of 3 S1 brief claims wrong on contact. For priority 4 it is the clearest mechanism in the set — one prompt buys 32 agents, 79 tool calls and 7m54s of unattended adversarial reading at 4 concurrent. It also passes the repo's own instrument test rather than failing it: 4 of 31 came back confirmed, so it is not a skeptic that can only refute, and it has a real FAIL control (a seeded false claim). Its ~1.98M subagent tokens per round is a priority-5 cost against a priority-1 benefit, which is the right side of this operator's order. The draft's one binding constraint is correct and must stay in the saved workflow's own text: evidence on disk, or the skeptics refute from priors.

PP3/PP1. The strongest argument is a number the draft owns but does not quote: the exact session windows show the wall arriving 1h20m, 1h37m and 2h28m into a five-hour window, with 512,180 out in 80 minutes on 2026-09-06. Elapsed time therefore predicts nothing, and a live rate_limits gauge is the only thing that lets the operator decide whether a fan-out launched now will finish — which is exactly the decision that produced the two confirmed post-block re-orientation episodes and the 57-to-211-minute resume lags. It is also the precondition for judging C8 and C2 at all, and for the one open question 13-research names as most valuable (cache-read's weight against the subscription limit, NOT FOUND anywhere). Held at 4 because every field is unverified payload; the draft's own first step — dump the raw JSON and read it before writing one conditional — is the only thing standing between this and another gate built on an unread mechanism.

PP5 is real and large: 97% of 76,259 requests at xhigh, workflow-subagent at 28.4% of all output (18,968,002 of 66.9M) on Opus. Lower-effort mechanical stages burn the five-hour window slower, which is a genuine second-order priority-4 gain given how early the walls arrive. The draft is also right to refuse CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL globally (pre-2.1.251 it outranks per-call model and frontmatter, and the PATH CLI is 2.1.92). Held at 3 on my lens for two ergonomics costs the draft does not price: per-stage model and effort is config surface added to every workflow script forever, in exchange for a priority-5/6 gain; and the proposed A/B (agreement on 5 of 6 candidates) cannot separate a real agreement rate from noise at n=6.

PP1 is measured on both ends — 282k cached tokens per main-lane request, 107 compactions all manual with none below 462,618 preTokens (p50 491,829), Fable's own session at 374k per request — and the meter to judge it already exists, so the experiment is free. But the payoff is explicitly unmeasured: 13-research lists cache-read's weighting against the subscription limit as NOT FOUND anywhere, so 'cache-read is where the tokens go' and 'cache-read is where the limit goes' are still different claims. On my lens it is neutral to negative for priority 4: a /clear seam starts a session that must read its way in, which is the same cost shape as the eleven post-block resumes this package spent a chapter measuring. Run it as the A/B the draft describes; do not write it into CLAUDE.md as a rule before the two-week comparison lands.

PP6's pain is the biggest single number in the package — 84.4M tokens of startup context across 2,682 spawns against 7.9M across 282 main sessions, 10.6x, with a frontier main-lane opening at 52,840 to 57,689 median — but 12-startup-cost.md states plainly that which of the system prompt, the 121-skill listing, the MCP definitions, CLAUDE.md or the memory index accounts for the ~53k 'cannot be answered from transcripts alone'. So the payoff of pruning is unmeasured and the A/B is the measurement, not the recommendation. The score splits: disabling claude-session-driver (hooks on every PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionStart/SessionEnd, emitting events for a csd worker-driver with no recorded use) is C1-grade ratio and should ship alongside C1 as one diff; the rest is a scratch-session experiment that should be labelled as one.

PP7 is the right target and this is the wrong instrument — it fails the house rule it is named after. The gate's own PASS control is #780, which the package names in PP7 as an instance of the failure class it is meant to prevent (release-health's unset-output guard, S5's total=0 hole). A check whose known-good input is a known-bad outcome cannot distinguish the two; it enforces the strings 'PASS' and 'FAIL' in a PR body, and the draft concedes 'it cannot read evidence; it enforces the habit, not the truth'. On my lens it is a pure attention tax: a blocking gate on every PR touching .github/workflows/**, src/audits/** and src/alerts/**, paid on every future PR, with no measured reduction in anything. C11 does the same job at the layer where the evidence actually is.

PP7, and the only candidate that automates detection of the class the census says no heuristic can see, with zero operator attention per night — priority 4 in its purest form, and priority 3 because a cockpit chip is read where the operator already looks. Its controls are the right shape and they vary: the 'Analytics soft-fail at' signal from #782 (never fired) must be listed, and FLEET_FORM_E2E skipped=N after #779 (varies) must not. Held at 4 rather than 5 on two counts: the measured instance rate is roughly five in a month (the 2026-08-12 trio, #782, #780/S5) against a day of build, and the ack-with-expiry the draft names as a mistake-guard is mandatory rather than optional — a nagging chip on a legitimate hard invariant is how the Prismic drift ack had to be invented in the first place.

PP8, and the pain is measured at approximately zero by this package's own refuter. Confirmed verdict i=29 states that the repeated /model turn is 'a mechanical model switch typed into three unrelated repos', that 'retyping a config command costs essentially no operator attention' and that it 'produced 0 tokens'. The draft's own mistake-if then concedes the switches may be keyed to the weekly reset rather than the repo — 26 of the 81 went to Fable after 'we just got a reset', which is a time key, not a repo key. It also spends an operator decision it does not need to: C12 ships only if the .claude/ tracking question (A9) resolves yes. Spending a decision from the six-a-day budget to save a keystroke measured as costless is the wrong trade under this order.

Correctly filed as priority 1 and explicitly not a token lever. The measurement is a count, not a behaviour: 1,020 permissions.allow entries and 43 additionalDirectories, including Bash(git reset:*) and Bash(for f:*), in a repo whose CLAUDE.md records two real concurrent-session collisions — a /loop that clobbered the main checkout's HEAD, and a paused session's branch taking another session's commit into its squash. The control is clean and reversible. On my lens it cuts both ways: 1,020 unreviewable entries is itself an ergonomics failure, but every allow removed is a prompt added, i.e. more stops per unattended hour, and 30 minutes of the scarcest resource in the package. Prune the dangerous verbs (git reset, the unbounded loop pattern) rather than attempting the 1,020.

Splits three ways and should be scored that way. (a) is the best minutes-to-value ratio in the whole set: one CLAUDE.md line against the single confirmed overload (2026-08-24, wasteShare 0.6, 'my system got overloaded and you didn't stop your agents') plus 'computer crashed because I also opened steam, resume' typed into four sessions — a confirmed same-turn-many-sessions group, which is pure operator attention. (b) is minutes and is the only mechanism in the package that keeps a session running with the lid closed, but 13-research's own caveat is that Remote Control is a foreground process killed by a reboot or ~10 minutes of network loss — a window onto one machine, not persistence. (c) should be dropped rather than deferred: the same document's Option B says a second machine 'cannot reach any relief from the binding constraint, because the ceiling here is the plan's usage limit rather than RAM', and it forces the credential question the sandbox currently answers by denying ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and ~/.config/reddoor-maint.

demote: C10 — ranked as serving priorities 1 and 3; it measurably serves neither. Its PASS control is #780, the same PR the package lists under PP7 as an instance of the instrument-blind failure class it is meant to catch, so the gate's known-good input is a known-bad outcome and it cannot separate the two. The draft concedes it 'cannot read evidence'. What it does deliver, on every PR touching .github/workflows/**, src/audits/** and src/alerts/**, is a blocking check satisfiable by typing two words — an attention tax with no measured return. C11 covers the same pain where the evidence lives.

C12 — ranked as serving priority 3 on the strength of '81 manual /model switches', but this package's own confirmed refuter verdict (i=29) kills the pain: retyping /model 'costs essentially no operator attention' and 'produced 0 tokens'. verdicts.reason:
C14 fails five of the six tests, and two of them are fatal on the cited evidence alone.

(b) The mechanism does not exist as described. C14(b) claims "Remote Control for the UI so the laptop lid can close on a session that stays local." 13-research.md:402 (Option A) says the opposite in the same file C14 cites: Remote Control from the current laptop "Cannot reach anything while the laptop is asleep, off the network for more than about ten minutes, or rebooted," because (13-research.md:266, :398) "the Remote Control process is a foreground process, so 'closing your terminal, rebooting, or losing network for ~10 minutes will kill the session.'" Closing the lid sleeps the Mac and kills the session. Remote Control the product is DOC-CONFIRMED (13-research.md:392, quoting remote-control.md:30-36) — its advertised benefit here is not. This is the draft's own PP4 failure (building on a mechanism without reading it) committed inside the recommendation against PP4.

(a)+(c) The pain is not measured as stated, and the mechanism does not address it. PP9's evidence reduces to two episodes. The one confirmed episode (census-refute.json i=25, CONFIRMED, `Broken` 2026-08-24T23:51Z) is six parallel agents; the skeptic's own words: "The genuinely avoidable decision — dispatching six parallel agents ... sits outside this window." The second ("computer crashed because I also opened steam") is census-refute.json i=27, verdict REFUTED, "unavoidable recovery ... The measured cost is 0 requests / 0 in / 0 out / 0 cache." So the measured cause of the one real overload is fan-out breadth, and the one crash was Steam. `grep -i "browser|chrome|playwright"` over 11-wasted-work-census.md returns nothing (only "Godot"); 10-token-meter.md and 12-startup-cost.md likewise carry no local-browser contention measurement. C14(a) — "never run Chrome/Playwright locally while agents run" — therefore treats an unmeasured cause and leaves both episodes untouched. Worse, its parenthetical is already the status quo: fleet browser work already runs on Actions runners (`.github/workflows/fleet-form-e2e.yml:50`, `fleet-smoke.yml:46`, `fleet-lighthouse.yml:40`, `daily-reports.yml:69`, `ci.yml:45` each run `playwright install --with-deps chromium`), so (a) is a CLAUDE.md line restating existing practice.

(d) The proof plan is not two-sided and not executable. C14 offers "for (a) PASS = a week with no local browser use while agents run and no overload; (c) is a report, not a proof." (b) has no proof at all; (c) explicitly none; (a) has no FAIL control and a PASS that cannot fail — overload is an n=1 event in a 30-day corpus, so an overload-free week is the expected outcome whether or not the rule is adopted. That is exactly PP7 / this repo's "prove the instrument before you trust its verdict" class: a green check built so it can never go red. It is also not runnable in §0's sandbox (a week of observation, plus hardware procurement for (c)).

(e) It trades priority 1 for priority 4. 13-research.md:404 on Option B: an always-on second machine "cannot reach any relief from the binding constraint, because the ceiling here is the plan's usage limit rather than RAM, and adding a machine that makes concurrency easier pushes on the variable measured at r=0.56," and P15 at :274 concludes "Adopt it for persistence, not for parallelism." C14(c) claims to serve 4 (work between prompts) by making concurrency easier — the same pedal the research's own Rejected section refuses for the orchestration plugin (:414, "Adding a layer that makes breadth easier is pushing the pedal already measured as the problem"). Priority 1 (no overload) outranks 4.

(f) Simpler mechanisms already in the draft do the job. C2 (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY=4`, one settings line) directly prevents "six parallel agents," and C3 verifies the stop runbook — the 08-24 window burned four of its six TaskStop calls on a `ToolSearch` to load the TaskStop schema (census-refute.json i=25). Both address the only confirmed PP9 episode; C14 addresses none of it at a cost of half a day plus hardware.

Salvage, if the operator wants anything from #776: it is Option C (routines / cloud for the scheduled fleet sweeps, 13-research.md §Off the laptop, DOC-CONFIRMED), which C14 does not propose, and which belongs in its own candidate with its own two-sided proof.
